pairs.subject: measurement-honesty
pairs.evidence: packages/producers/src/publish/standing.ts:31 A channel's standing is folded over at most 200 ledger rows (`LIMIT ?`, WINDOW=200), and the limit is applied before dry rehearsals are filtered out. So once a success falls outside that window, `failuresSinceSuccess` is only a floor and `lastSuccessAt=null` reads as "never worked". Standing has no field that marks the truncation, so `pipeline/publish.mts:167` prints "last ok — · N failure(s) since" as if it were the total. Because DRY is the default, 200 dry rehearsals are enough to push the last live success out of the window.

techniques.evidence: packages/producers/src/publish/standing.ts:31 The floor is admitted only in a doc comment. The value that travels (Standing) has no truncated or at-least field, so consumers render the count as a total.

packages/producers/src/publish/standing.ts:57 The listing is capped by LIMIT, and nothing checks whether it was truncated before standingOf interprets it. A full window with no success turns into the verdict lastSuccessAt=null.

packages/producers/src/publish/metrics.ts:31 Metrics the platform does not report are null, not 0. A withheld or deleted video arrives as null (lib/publish/youtube.ts fetchStats maps missing ids to null), and the note names the mechanism at metrics.ts:77.
packages/producers/src/publish/metrics.ts:18 This context only appends snapshots. Totals and group sums are computed in @gt/domain/publication, so no averaging happens here.
packages/producers/src/publish/metrics.ts:26 No rate or percentage is derived anywhere in the context. It reports raw counts and lifetime totals only.
packages/producers/src/publish/metrics.ts:46 No comparison or control arm exists here. This line shows the related honest move: when metrics are not measured, a reason is reported instead of zeros.

pairs.registryProposal: incomplete-not-verdict lists truncated listings as an ingestion-boundary case. A capped fold over an event log (a fixed SELECT … LIMIT window used to derive a "since last success" streak) is the same defect inside one query, and lower-bound-disclosure could name it as a typical floor: a streak counted inside a bounded window.
